source.title: Ghost Noise for Regularizing Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Atli Kosson; Dongyang Fan; Martin Jaggi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own experiments on batch-size-dependent normalization and noise regularization, including conditions that improve or degrade test performance; it refines the generalization-gap account through train-test discrepancy and ghost noise. Its results do not test most other claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests regularization methods and batch-normalization behavior, not memorization of random labels, width beyond interpolation, optimizer comparisons, explicit dropout or weight-decay effects as stated in the versions, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. GBN, XBN, GNI, dropout comparisons, normalization-free settings, and architecture/dataset extensions have reported results. Prior-work claims in the introduction and related work are not extracted as this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The dropout-probability sweep in Figure 3 tests V6 in a ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 setting, even though dropout serves as a comparator. Its outcome relative to no dropout cannot be established from the supplied figure text. The normalization and ghost-noise experiments do not test V5: they change normalization statistics or injected noise without comparing optimizer batch sizes.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that ghost noise supplies useful regularization; GNI separates this noise from small-batch normalization and reduces self-dependency-related train-test discrepancy. They report benefits across several architectures and normalization settings, contributions from both shift and scale noise, and channel- and layer-dependent noise distributions.
record.recipe_differences: Studies batch-normalization ghost noise and proposes XBN and GNI; it does not use the claim's random-label memorization, width, optimizer, large accelerator-batch, or sharpness methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Ghost batch size changes validation/test performance; XBN is unstable below 32; GNI benefits vary by architecture, dataset, augmentation setting, normalization type, and selected ghost batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Changing normalization batch size changes accuracy at fixed optimizer batch size. On CIFAR-100, GBN-16 reaches 78.20% versus BN's 77.10%; on ImageNet, GBN-16 and GBN-32 underperform BN.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Smaller normalization batches can improve generalization, with benefits depending on dataset and normalization-induced train-test discrepancy.

fits_no_version.finding: GNI improves held-out accuracy across the reported normalization settings and architectures, including settings without batch normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably tuned ghost-noise injection can improve image-classifier generalization independently of reducing optimizer batch size.

record.peer_reviewed: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (accepted to AAAI 2024; venue field states 2023)
record.problems: The authors state repeated experiments limit the size and number of settings explored; most work focuses on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100 and detailed ablations are unavailable across wider settings. Several results are figures without exact values in the supplied text. The paper does not compare accelerator batch sizes for V5; its batch-size sweeps concern normalization ghost batch size.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Rows report the paper's own relevant normalization/noise outcomes. Comparisons in cited prior work are not included as this study's results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons under limited or broader tuning.
All parts: no optimizer-batch-size sweep establishes a large-batch penalty or its removal.
Very small training sets, demonstrated underfitting from excessive dropout, fully connected classifiers, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removal of memorized examples compared with random removal.

missing.what: Separate dropout-versus-zero-dropout outcomes for Bernoulli/Gaussian and elementwise/channelwise variants across the probability sweep. R20 aggregates these conditions and reports only their ranking against other regularizers; numerical curves are unavailable in the supplied text.
missing.locator: Figure 3, lower-right panel; Section 4.1, GNI vs Dropout

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V5 limits_scope verdict: an untested optimizer-batch comparison cannot establish a scope limit. V6 is tested, but no directional verdict is justified from the supplied text: dropout's inferiority to GNI does not establish its effect relative to no dropout. States of cannot_determine on rows linked to none concern the listed claims, not whether the reported normalization/noise gains occurred.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local-connectivity comparisons.

Large versus small accelerator/optimizer batches under fixed epoch budgets, learning-rate scaling and warmup remedies, and language models. The paper varies normalization ghost batch size, not accelerator batch size.
Dropout versus no dropout and the small-training-set and underfitting regimes. Dropout is compared as a distinct regularizer, not tested as the claimed intervention.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100; ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10; ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1k; listed architectural extensions
reader_labels.reason: The study varies ghost batch size while keeping accelerator batch size 256, so it does not directly test the fixed-epoch large accelerator-batch claim; outcomes also differ across dataset and normalization settings (R1-R19, R21-R27). GBN lowers ImageNet-1k accuracy at ghost batch sizes 16 and 32 relative to BN-256 (R14-R15).
